summary: Boone County steel lookout, about 110 ft, described by NGS in 1961; the source page marks it removed with no year.

facts.design: four-legged steel tower with a gray metal observation room at the top
facts.status_note: Marked removed on the source page; no removal year given

events.note: NGS station description places the standing tower in 1961

evidence.supports: About 3-3/4 miles southwest of Omaha, in Boone County
evidence.quote: LOCATED ABOUT 3-3/4 MILES SOUTHWEST OF OMAHA, IN THE SOUTHWEST
IT IS A FOUR LEGGED STEEL

evidence.supports: Gray metal observation room at the top
evidence.quote: STRUCTURE WITH A GREY METAL OBSERVATION ROOM AT ITS TOP.
THE OVERALL HEIGHT IS ABOUT 110 FEET.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1961 (BRB)

evidence.supports: Height of fire tower use 1930s to 1970s; more than 120 towers
evidence.quote: At the height of their use (1930s to 1970s), Arkansas had more than 120 fire towers

evidence.supports: Aerial surveillance reduced the need for lookout towers
evidence.quote: With aerial surveillance (and later, satellites), the need for lookout towers diminished.

notes_for_editor: Only one tower-specific page (Forest Lookouts) plus statewide context from the Encyclopedia of Arkansas. Two web searches found nothing on Burlington's build date, staffing, fires or current site. height_m is converted from 110 feet. The page's removal year is not given, so no removed event is recorded. The NGS directions (from the Omaha post office on US 65, then 2.05 miles north on gravel) were left out: they describe a 1961 route to a removed site of unknown access. Brief status 'gone' is supported; no corrections. The firelookout.org Arkansas listing returned 404; the NHLR and FFLOS caches have no entry for this tower. Encyclopedia (46 standing in 2023) and Preserve Arkansas ('about 40' remain) disagree on statewide counts; neither is used in the story.
